citations.quote:
Assume countable choice. Take a balanced multipointed diagram for one oriented knot in $S^3$ with the splitting, compression disks and cyclic marking convention of the balanced pointed-data definition, without assuming its admissibility. Write $A_i$ and $B_i$ for the components of the complements of the two attaching systems, numbered so that $w_i,z_i\in A_i$ and $w_i,z_{i+1}\in B_i$, with cyclic indices, $1\le i\le k$.

Every integral domain $P$ whose boundary is an integral sum of full attaching curves has an integral representation
$$P=\sum_{i=1}^k a_iA_i+\sum_{i=1}^k b_iB_i.$$
If $n_{w_i}(P)=0$ for every $i$, then $b_i=-a_i$ and
$$n_{z_i}(P)=a_i-a_{i-1},\qquad \sum_i n_{z_i}(P)=0.$$
Such a domain is zero if all its $z$ multiplicities vanish. Consequently every nonzero such domain has both a positive and a negative region coefficient: the diagram is admissible in the precise periodic-domain sense of that Definition. In particular every balanced knot diagram appearing in a valid knot-preserving multipointed move sequence in $S^3$ is admissible, without a further winding modification. This assertion does not construct the move sequence or analytic moduli spaces.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U$ be a connected oriented smooth handlebody with genus-$h$ boundary $\Sigma$, and let $m=h+k-1>0$ disjoint proper compression disks cut it into $k\ge1$ balls. Broad smooth boundary tangencies of these auxiliary disks are permitted. Write $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_m$ for their boundary circles and $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ for the components of $\Sigma\setminus\bigcup\gamma_j$. Fix ANY orientation-compatible Riemann surface structure $j$ on $\Sigma$ and put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ and $L=q(\gamma_1\times\cdots\times\gamma_m)$.

For every actual smooth based disk $u:(\overline{\mathbb D},\partial\mathbb D,p)\to(X,L,x)$, let its domain be the componentwise relative point-divisor degrees
$$D(u)=\sum_{i=1}^k b_i A_i,\qquad b_i\in\mathbb Z.$$
Its boundary Maslov index satisfies
$$\mu_L(u)=2\sum_{i=1}^k b_i.$$
This includes all signed multiplicities and all realized smooth relative classes. If $k\ge2$, each unit component domain $A_i$ is itself realized by an explicitly constructed smooth based disk at ANY $x\in L$, of boundary Maslov index two; this is not an assertion of a holomorphic representative.

Every actual compact geometric Cauchy--Riemann-symbol operator along $u$ has real index $m+2\sum b_i$. In the bounded point-trace realizations $H^{q+1}\to H^q$, $q\ge2$, imposing its fixed boundary-node value subtracts $m$ and gives index $2\sum b_i$. The same indices hold for any autonomous nearly symmetric tame structure equal to $\operatorname{Sym}^m(j)$ near the diagonal, with its actual boundary torus totally real; the comparison homotopy is proved below. No ordinary $H^1$ point trace is used.

In particular an actual nonconstant holomorphic boundary disk of Maslov index two, in the protected nearly symmetric class for which compact-domain positivity holds, has domain EXACTLY one $A_i$. This proves the domain/index classification only: it computes neither its count nor its regularity or attachment gluing. For $k=1$ it asserts the index of every realized class without asserting a nonzero-degree sphere or disk exists. For the omitted point target $h=0,k=1,m=0$, every actual map is constant, its divisor domain and index are zero.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed oriented Riemann surface with an actual finite oriented polygon as in the sphere-index theorem, $m\ge1$, and put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$. Let $\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta$ be two disjoint-within-system smooth curve families of size $m$, transverse to each other, with product tori $L_\alpha,L_\beta$. Give two smooth fixed-end Whitney disk models $u,v$ from the same generator $x$ to the same generator $y$, constant near their two marked boundary corners, with their actual fixed product end data. Use the auxiliary complex-structure homotopies and actual relative-index realizations specified in the relative Whitney index theorem. Domain coefficients mean the integer relative degrees of the point-divisor lines, not a holomorphic representative assumption.

For any such pair, $D(u)-D(v)$ has boundary a sum of full attaching circles. The coefficient on each oriented circle is the angular winding difference of the corresponding labelled boundary paths, with their source-boundary signs. In particular, if $D(u)=D(v)$ as region chains, their boundary paths on each labelled alpha circle are homotopic relative their endpoints, and likewise on each labelled beta circle. After these boundary homotopies the difference of their smooth relative classes is represented by a sphere $A$ with $n_z(A)=0$. Consequently
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}(u)=\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}(v),$$
before source translation, on all the stated higher Sobolev and allowed smooth weighted realizations. Thus actual Fredholm index is well defined on the set of REALIZED Whitney domains, including classes with positive, zero or negative marked multiplicities. No assertion that every integer region chain is realized is made.

The analogous statement holds for two smooth disks based at the same point of a single product torus $L_\gamma$, with equal one-system domains: their boundary loops are based homotopic, and their boundary Maslov indices and compact-disk Fredholm indices agree. Their fixed-node indices also agree whenever that bounded point-trace realization is used. The finite polygon hypothesis is supplied for the original embedded balanced $S^3$ data by the broad-input application in the sphere-index theorem. No full formula $e(D)+n_x(D)+n_y(D)$, normalized relative or absolute grading, invariance, or arbitrary-domain representativity is included.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed oriented genus-$h$ Riemann surface with a supplied orientation-compatible finite polygon presentation as in the finite diagonal-degree theorem, and let $m\ge1$. Put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$. For every smooth sphere map $u:S^2\to X$ and every $z\in\Sigma$, define $n_z(u)$ to be the degree of $u^*\mathcal O(E_z)$, where $E_z=\{z\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$ and degree is finite face winding, including when the sphere image is contained in $E_z$. Then
$$\deg(u^*\det_{\mathbb C}TX)=(m+1-h)n_z(u).$$
In particular this formula is valid for arbitrary smooth sphere classes, not only holomorphic maps or simple incidence curves. It is unchanged on replacing the standard complex tangent bundle by a homotopic complex structure on the same real tangent bundle.

Let a smooth fixed-end Whitney strip model with actual product end frames represent a class $\phi$, and let $\phi\#u$ be its interior connected sum with such a sphere, using a specified attaching path and keeping the physical boundary and end data fixed. Its actual real Fredholm indices, before source translation, satisfy
$$\mu(\phi\#u)-\mu(\phi)=2(m+1-h)n_z(u).$$
Thus when $m=h+k-1$ the sphere shift is exactly $2k\,n_z(u)$. This includes all positive and negative sphere degrees. In particular the finite polygon can be constructed, rather than separately supplied, when $\Sigma$ bounds a smooth handlebody embedded in $S^3$ with $m=h+k-1$ smooth proper rank-two compression disks cutting it topologically into $k$ balls. This application permits tangential disk boundaries: auxiliary disk replacement and smooth cut-ball reconstruction are proved prerequisites below. No full domain/corner formula for a nonspherical Whitney class, boundary-degeneration count, absolute grading or invariance theorem is included.

Assume countable choice. Let $X$ be a compact smooth manifold with a smooth path $J_t$ of almost complex structures, and let $L_0,L_1$ be compact submanifolds totally real for $J_0,J_1$, respectively. Suppose their intersection is finite and transverse. At each intersection point choose a target chart in which $L_0=\mathbb R^m$, $L_1=i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t=i$ for every $t$. Retain those same charts and structures throughout.

A smooth fixed-end representative from $x$ to $y$ is a smooth map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ with boundary on $L_0,L_1$, identically $x$ on one full negative tail and identically $y$ on one full positive tail. Its covariant Cauchy–Riemann linearization on fixed-end $H^1\to L^2$ spaces is Fredholm. Its real index is independent of the chosen smooth connection and of the representative under any smooth relative homotopy $H(h,s,t)$ with those boundary conditions, fixed endpoints, and one common pair of constant tails for all $h\in[0,1]$.

These indices add under concatenating two such representatives at their common endpoint, are zero for a constant representative, and change sign when $u(s,t)$ is replaced by $u(-s,t)$. Thus they define an integer index on smooth fixed-end representatives modulo the stated smooth relative homotopies, with concatenation and reversal laws. This result includes nonholomorphic representatives. It does not assume that a nonlinear moduli space exists or is regular.

A further relative smoothing and end-flattening argument is required to identify this smooth quotient with a Whitney-class set defined initially by arbitrary continuous disk maps and continuous relative homotopies. No such identification, domain Euler formula, or arbitrary-class representativity theorem is asserted here.

Assume countable choice. Retain the compact target, totally real boundary submanifolds, fixed path $J_t$ and exact product generator charts of the smooth relative-homotopy index lemma. A continuous Whitney representative from $x$ to $y$ is a continuous disk map with two specified boundary points mapped to $x,y$ and its two boundary arcs mapped into $L_0,L_1$. Equivalence means an actual continuous relative homotopy fixing those points and preserving the two boundary conditions.

Every such class has a smooth fixed-end strip representative, constant on full tails. If two smooth fixed-end representatives are continuously relatively homotopic, there is a smooth relative homotopy between them with one common pair of constant tails and the same fixed endpoints. Consequently the quotient of smooth fixed-end representatives by those smooth homotopies identifies with the continuous Whitney-class set. The actual real Fredholm index of its fixed-end Cauchy–Riemann-symbol linearization therefore defines an integer $\mu(\phi)$ on every continuous Whitney class; it agrees with the actual index of each smooth fixed-end model, is additive under class concatenation, is zero on the constant class, and changes sign under reversal.

For an actual smooth finite-energy holomorphic strip with uniform generator ends, its actual Fredholm index equals this index of its continuously compactified Whitney class.

This proves a continuous-class index using genuine representatives and relative homotopies. It does not identify that integer with a domain Euler measure, corner multiplicities or a first-Chern pairing; no nonlinear moduli counts or their regularity are asserted.

derivations.claim: Use [F4] to take smooth fixed-end models for $u,v$, with common constant tails. Their domain difference is periodic by the full-curve winding assertion [F3]. Thus [F1] gives $P=D(u)-D(v)=\sum a_iA_i+\sum b_iB_i$. Evaluation at the actual cyclic marks gives both total marked differences equal to $s=\sum a_i+\sum b_i$, including when several marks lie in one region. No positivity or index restriction is used in this identity of integral chains. [F1, F3, F4, given, construct, algebra]

We give the boundary insertion comparison needed here explicitly. Let $d$ be a smooth disk based at a generator $x$ on either one of its product tori. Flatten a small boundary interval at its node to the constant $x$ by a real scalar cutoff in a smooth adapted torus chart. Flatten a small interval on the corresponding horizontal edge of the constant negative tail of $v$ in the same way; that tail is already constant. Remove the two constant intervals and join their collars, reversing the induced interval orientations. The oriented boundary connected sum of the strip rectangle and the disk is again a strip rectangle with the same distinguished ends. A finite smooth collar parametrization and rounding give an actual smooth fixed-end map. On the joined collars the map is constant, and on all other horizontal edges it has the required torus boundary. This works on either horizontal side. In both cases the disk inherits its ORIGINAL source orientation: oriented boundary gluing reverses the interval orientations, rather than reflecting the disk. Hence relative divisor degrees add with a PLUS sign on both sides. In determinant frames constant near the gluing interval the physical real tangent phases there are identical. The two copies of that constant interval cancel, while the inserted disk contributes its positively traversed squared phase loop. The end caps are untouched. Consequently the new strip index is $\mu(v)+\mu_L(d)$, on either the alpha or beta side. This is a boundary winding calculation, not a holomorphic gluing or regularity assertion. [F3, F4, construct, algebra]

Suppose $k\ge2$. Insert the actual based unit disks of [F2] at the negative constant tail, $a_i$ times on the alpha side and $b_i$ times on the beta side. For negative exponents precompose the disk by a reflection fixing its node; this reverses both its domain degree and its boundary phase. There are finitely many insertions, whose constant intervals may be chosen disjoint or successive. Step 1.2 gives an actual model $v_P$ with domain $D(v)+P=D(u)$ and index $\mu(v_P)=\mu(v)+2s$. The equal-domain assertion [F3] therefore gives $\mu(u)=\mu(v_P)$. Together with step 1.1 this proves both marked-degree formulas. The construction realizes only the periodic correction already given by [F1]; it does not assert realization of an arbitrary nonperiodic formal chain. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

If $k=1$, [F1] instead says $P=c\Sigma$. Every coefficient jump is zero. By [F3] each labelled boundary-path difference has zero angular winding, so real argument lifts give alpha and beta boundary homotopies relative endpoints. Glue $u$, those torus cylinders, and the orientation reversal of $v$ to an actual sphere, smoothing the constant seams as in [F3]. Its divisor degree is $c$, since the boundary cylinders avoid the point divisor. Here $m=h$, so its determinant degree is $c$ by [F3]. Comparing the two disk frames across the cylinders leaves twice this sphere clutch degree as the difference of the physical capped boundary phase windings. Thus $\mu(u)-\mu(v)=2c$, while each total marked difference is $c$. This case uses only an actual sphere obtained from the given classes; it presumes no sphere of any other degree exists. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

Taking $v$ to be the actual constant model proves the same-generator assertion, using its zero domain and zero index from [F4]. Steps 2.1 and 2.2 show the two endpoint-dependent quantities are independent of the realized class. The passage back to continuous classes and to actual holomorphic linearizations is exactly [F4]; no formal-domain index or Euler/corner expression has replaced that actual index. For $m=0$ the target is a point and all the claimed degrees and indices are zero directly. All constructions beyond the stated Countable Choice suppliers were finite. [F4, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

Step 2.2 treats k1 using an actual sphere cap, without presuming any nonzero sphere exists.
Steps 1.1 and 1.2 fix both endpoint generators and their caps, including shared coordinates.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 realizes negative coefficients by orientation reversal. Step 1.2 explicitly reverses gluing interval orientations, preserving disk source orientation on either side and adding its physical phase with positive sign.
Step 3.1 uses only finite constructions beyond the declared Countable Choice suppliers.
